sections.h2: How does the lake affect selling a house in St. Clair Shores?
sections.html:
Lake St. Clair touches nearly every part of a St. Clair Shores sale, from canal and lakefront houses to the flood-zone check that follows insurance quotes. Water covers close to 19 percent of the city, and part of the city lies in the FEMA floodplain, so learn your own address's status early.

The city sits in southern Macomb County on the lake's western shore, about 14 miles northeast of downtown Detroit, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 57,872 residents. Three selling routes are common:

  • A listing with an agent fits a well-kept house and an owner willing to wait out a buyer's loan.
  • A sale by owner saves the commission and leaves contracts and title steps to you.
  • A cash sale as-is suits deferred repairs, tenants or an estate. Compare offers and note who covers which closing costs.

sections.h2: What is St. Clair Shores like for a seller?
sections.html:
The city measures 14.40 square miles overall, with 2.72 of them water. Wikipedia reports about 14 miles of canals, most along the Nautical Mile, the Jefferson Avenue strip between 9 Mile and 10 Mile Roads that holds restaurants, boat dealers and marinas. The 28-story Shore Club Sky Tower, at the foot of Nine Mile Road, is the tallest structure in town.

French settlers arrived as early as 1710, and farms dominated until the early 1900s. The village formed in 1925, and residents chose cityhood in January 1951. Wikipedia says many subdivisions were platted early but built out only after World War II, making this Detroit's fastest-growing suburb in the 1950s. Jefferson Beach Amusement Park ran on the lakefront from 1927 to 1959.

Youth hockey is a local tradition, with two municipal ice arenas at the civic recreation center. Interstate 94 skirts the western edge through exits 224 to 230, about 13 miles from midtown Detroit.

Population peaked decades ago. The census counted 63,096 residents in 2000, 59,715 in 2010 and 58,874 in 2020, while land density eased from 5,139.5 to 5,040.2 people per square mile between 2010 and 2020. During Prohibition the lakefront village was known for roadhouses and rum running, and the Miss St. Clair Shores scholarship program has run since 1953.

Neighbors matter when you describe a location. Roseville and Eastpointe lie to the west, and Harper Woods, Grosse Pointe Woods and Grosse Pointe Shores lie to the south across the Wayne County line. The area was part of Erin Township from 1843 to 1911 and then of Lake Township, so older records for the city may carry those names. Ask the title company to search under them if a document looks incomplete.

sections.h2: How does the floodplain affect a St. Clair Shores sale?
sections.html:
The city's flood page explains that FEMA redraws its maps now and then, so a parcel once in the floodplain may now be outside it, and the reverse can happen. Buyers often ask about flood status, since insurers and lenders look at it.

The city names two lookup tools:

  • Macomb County GIS: type the address, open Layers, expand Natural Features and tick Flood Zones. A parcel that turns red may be in the zone.
  • FEMA's flood map search by street address.

If an insurer has placed the house in the floodplain and you hold a survey or other evidence against it, you may qualify for a Letter of Map Amendment, or you can use the city's Options to Appeal Determination form. Sorting this out before listing spares you a surprise during a buyer's loan review.

sections.h2: Which school districts and roads do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Three public districts share the city. South Lake Schools covers the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north, and each runs a high school inside the city limits. Ask the districts to confirm a specific address, because buyers want that detail.

Private options include St. Isaac Jogues and St. Joan of Arc, while St. Germaine closed in 2024. Wikipedia credits the city's popularity to its lakefront, park system, recreation programs and choice of districts.

I-94 and Jefferson Avenue carry most commuters. Census puts the average trip to work at 26.7 minutes, the longest among these four cities.

sections.h2: What do St. Clair Shores rules say about rental houses?
sections.html:
The city wants every non-owner-occupied house registered and holding a certificate of approval before anyone moves in. Its registration form prints these terms:

  • Single-family house: $150 for the first 3,000 square feet, then $10 for each added 1,000 square feet.
  • Multiple-family building: $150 for the first unit, then $50 for each added unit in that building.
  • The fee pays for the first inspection and one follow-up. A rescheduled visit when nobody is on site costs $30, and a failed-compliance reinspection costs half the original fee.
  • An owner who lives beyond Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Washtenaw and St. Clair counties must name a local agent.
  • Once the house sells, send the city a recorded deed or land contract to be dropped from its records.

Community Development and Inspections, at 586-447-3340, can confirm what applies to your address and whether an open permit needs closing before a sale.

sections.h2: What will the Macomb County recorder charge me?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds in Mount Clemens, on N. Main Street, records deeds for a $30 fee however many pages they run. Of that amount, $4 supports the state survey and remonumentation fund. Call (586) 469-7953 with questions.

A tax certificate from the County Treasurer must come first for warranty deeds and land contracts, along with their covenant-clause and assignment variants. The fee page lists it at $5 for up to five legal descriptions.

The county's transfer tax table multiplies the sale price by 0.0075 for the state and by 0.0011 for the county. Your title company can turn those rates into a dollar total at your price.

Treasury's ownership FAQ adds that the buyer reports the change of ownership to the assessor on Form 2766 inside 45 days.

faqs.q: Is my St. Clair Shores house in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Check Macomb County GIS or FEMA's flood map search, both linked by the city. Part of the city is in the FEMA floodplain, and a survey that shows otherwise may support a Letter of Map Amendment.

faqs.q: What do recording and transfer tax cost on a Macomb sale?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 per document. The county schedule lists state transfer tax at 0.0075 of the sale price and county tax at 0.0011.

faqs.q: Do rental houses have to be registered in St. Clair Shores?
faqs.a: Yes. Registration and a certificate of approval come before occupancy, and a single-family house starts at $150 for the first 3,000 square feet.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my street?
faqs.a: South Lake Schools serves the south, Lakeview Public Schools the middle and Lake Shore Public Schools the north. Confirm your address with the district.
Wikipedia gives 14.40 square miles in total, with 2.72 of water, while the Census Bureau lists 11.68 square miles of land. The 2020 census counted 58,874 residents.
